item.text:
## 3B.1 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024

**Assessment:** Mostly **no**. The 2024 record shows continuing arbitrary detention, impunity for abuses in Manipur and Jammu & Kashmir, politicized prosecutions, and coercive policing. There is some weak counterevidence in the form of NHRC action and official claims of justice reform, but I found **no direct Modi-led accountability** for security-force abuse.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [India: Increased Abuses Against Minorities, Critics](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/india-increased-abuses-against-minorities-critics) | Human Rights Watch | 11 Jan 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/india-increased-abuses-against-minorities-critics | HRW says BJP-led authorities stigmatized minorities, used politically motivated charges against critics, and that Manipur violence, internet shutdowns, and police failures persisted. This is strong evidence **against** 3B.1. | 3B.1 |
| [India: Authorities ‘missing-in-action’ amid ongoing violence and impunity in Manipur state](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/india-authorities-missing-in-action-amid-ongoing-violence-and-impunity-in-manipur-state-new-testimonies/) | Amnesty International | 16 Jul 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/india-authorities-missing-in-action-amid-ongoing-violence-and-impunity-in-manipur-state-new-testimonies/ | Amnesty says the BJP-led state and central governments failed to end the violence, protect displaced residents, or hold vigilante groups accountable in Manipur. This is direct evidence of **failure to protect residents from state-linked and surrounding violence**. | 3B.1 |
| [India: Repression Persists in Jammu and Kashmir](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/31/india-repression-persists-jammu-and-kashmir) | Human Rights Watch | 31 Jul 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/31/india-repression-persists-jammu-and-kashmir | HRW says Indian security forces continued arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, and other serious abuses in Jammu and Kashmir, with little accountability and long detentions under draconian laws. This is strong counterevidence. | 3B.1 |
| [Internet suspended in parts of India’s Manipur as students clash with police](https://theprint.in/india/internet-suspended-in-parts-of-indias-manipur-as-students-clash-with-police/2261451/) | Reuters feed via ThePrint | 10 Sep 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/internet-suspended-in-parts-of-indias-manipur-as-students-clash-with-police/2261451/ | Reuters reported tear gas, stun grenades, curfews, and internet/mobile shutdowns in Manipur after protests over ethnic violence and security failures. The state’s response was coercive crowd control, not resident protection. | 3B.1 |
| [India: Police Raid Rights Group in Delhi](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/04/india-police-raid-rights-group-delhi) | Human Rights Watch | 4 Dec 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/04/india-police-raid-rights-group-delhi | HRW says Delhi police raided APCR in a politically motivated action tied to criticism of hate speech and detained activists under UAPA. This supports a finding of **political repression** rather than protection. | 3B.1 |

This is **official positive self-claim** of reform, but it does not offset the abuse record on its own. | 3B.1 |
| [NHRC takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of 12 inmates within a month in the Delhi government-run Shelter Home- Asha Kiran in Rohini](https://nhrc.nic.in/media/press-release/nhrc-india-takes-suo-motu-cognizance-the-reported-death-12-inmates-within-a-month-in-the-delhi-government-run-shelter-home-asha-kiran-in-rohini) | National Human Rights Commission | 3 Aug 2024 | https://nhrc.nic.in/media/press-release/nhrc-india-takes-suo-motu-cognizance-the-reported-death-12-inmates-within-a-month-in-the-delhi-government-run-shelter-home-asha-kiran-in-rohini | NHRC took suo motu cognizance of multiple deaths in a Delhi shelter home and demanded a report and action against responsible officials. This shows **some accountability machinery** still functioned, but it is reactive and not Modi-led protection. | 3B.1 |

### Bottom line
- **Negative overall:** 2024 evidence points to continued arbitrary detention, coercive policing, impunity, and politically motivated prosecution.
- **Weak positives:** NHRC intervention and official reform claims exist, but I found no direct evidence that Modi personally accepted responsibility or meaningfully corrected abuses.

### Search gap
- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** of Modi publicly acknowledging responsibility for security-force torture, disappearances, or extrajudicial killings.
- I also found **no clear 2024 evidence** of a successful, Modi-led remedial shift that materially reduced these abuses during the year.
- The best-supported reading is **continued failure to protect residents**, with only limited institutional checks and self-described reform rhetoric.
